drug_profiles.mechanism: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing; normal tissues can also be affected. Kidney protection and assessment of hearing and nerves are essential during cisplatin treatment.

drug_profiles.name: Carboplatin
drug_profiles.mechanism: Carboplatin forms links in DNA that hinder copying and repair. Healthy tissues can also be harmed. Its dose depends on target exposure (AUC) and measured or estimated kidney function; AUC is not a fixed number of milligrams. There are two planned doses in this regimen.

drug_profiles.name: Vinorelbine
drug_profiles.mechanism: Vinorelbine disrupts the cell structures that help divide chromosomes. This can slow cancer growth and also affect blood cells, nerves and the bowel.

drug_profiles.name: Paclitaxel
drug_profiles.mechanism: Paclitaxel stabilises microtubules, structures cells use during division. It can slow cancer growth but also harm healthy nerves, blood-forming cells and hair follicles. Both medicines are planned on Day 1 of each of four cycles.

drug_profiles.name: Pemetrexed
drug_profiles.mechanism: Pemetrexed blocks several enzymes that use folate to make the building blocks of DNA and RNA. This can slow or stop cancer-cell growth. Healthy cells can also be affected. Prescribed folic acid and vitamin B12 reduce important toxicities and are part of treatment.

drug_profiles.name: Etoposide
drug_profiles.mechanism: Etoposide interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme that helps manage DNA during copying. DNA breaks can remain unrepaired and cancer cells may stop dividing or die. Healthy cells are also affected; the infusion or prescribed capsules deliver the same medicine by different routes.
